transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been having a really hard time engaging in any hobbies or leisure activities quietly. Even when I try to relax, read, or play a game, I
When you try to relax or do quiet activities, is it mostly because your mind is filled with excessive worries, or because you feel restless and have trouble staying still and focused?

It’s definitely more about feeling restless and having trouble staying still or focused. I don't really have excessive worries, but I just feel this constant physical need to be moving or doing something instead of sitting quietly.
Besides feeling restless, do you also often have trouble paying attention, finishing tasks, or staying organized in daily life?

No, I don't really have trouble with paying attention, finishing tasks, or staying organized. I am actually pretty good at getting things done once I start. My main struggle is just that I can't seem to do anything quietly or stay still.
Have you been this restless and unable to stay still since childhood, or did it start later in life?
Yes, I've actually been like this since I was a kid. I can remember feeling this restless and having trouble staying still well before I turned 12.
Has this restlessness caused problems in more than one setting, like at school or work and also at home or with friends?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really paid close attention to whether it happens across all of those different places or if it's just worse in some than others.
Can you think of specific examples of this restlessness causing trouble at school or work, and also separately at home or with friends?

At work, my excessive talking and tendency to interrupt colleagues during discussions causes a lot of friction. At home and with friends, I struggle to stay quiet during relaxed activities like watching movies, and I often butt into their conversations and games without meaning to.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a hyperactive/impulsive ADHD presentation: longstanding restlessness since childhood, inability to engage quietly in leisure activities, excessive talking, and interrupting others, with impairment at work and in home/social settings. Inattentive symptoms were denied, making the predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentation the best fit.
